problem_type: On Windows the agent panel cannot send any message: every conversation is filtered out of the lane list
symptom: Windows, real apimart key, new project, pick DeepSeek V4 Pro in the agent panel, type a message and click send: nothing happens. The text stays in the composer, the header conversation switcher shows 「—」, no error in the panel, renderer console or main log. The pushed workspace projection has active.lane = 'main' and lanes = []. tests/agent-runtime/lane-multi.test.mts is 4/5 red on Windows with agent_lane_conversation_missing.
direct_cause: laneSessionCwd gives each conversation the identity '/nomi-lane/<name>' and pi writes it into the session header as the session cwd after FileSystem.absolutePath, which NodeExecutionEnv implements as path.resolve(projectDir, cwd). On Windows that yields '<project drive>:\nomi-lane\main'. listLaneSessions only accepts headers whose cwd starts with '/nomi-lane/', so the new session is never listed; laneConversationOf returns null; laneClient.prepareInput returned null and the panel's send returned false without a message.
class_root: Two defects of one kind. (1) A virtual identity was handed to a host-path resolver on the assumption that an absolute POSIX string passes through path.resolve unchanged, which holds only on POSIX; nothing below the identity owner kept it verbatim. (2) The admission step expressed 'cannot admit input' as a silent null, so a broken workspace looked like a no-op click. Both went unseen because agent-runtime tests never run on Windows (82% of users per win-gate.yml).
affected_population: Every Windows user of a build containing fd77e800e (multi-conversation lanes, 2026-09-08), i.e. the withdrawn v0.22.0: the agent panel in every project, creation / generation / preview surfaces alike
Projects synced between macOS and Windows: the same conversation had two identities and two slug directories depending on the platform that wrote it
Not affected: macOS and Linux (path.resolve leaves '/nomi-lane/<name>' unchanged); v0.21.0 and earlier (no lane identity)
entry_points: openLaneSession (create or reopen the session of a lane; header cwd written here)
listLaneSessions (lane list in every workspace projection)

external_sources.purpose: path.resolve prepends the current drive on Windows for a root-relative path ('/foo' → 'C:\foo'); verified locally: path.resolve('C:\\proj', '/nomi-lane/main') = 'C:\nomi-lane\main', path.posix.resolve gives '/nomi-lane/main'.

pi-agent-core (installed dist/harness/env/nodejs.js:325) implements NodeExecutionEnv.absolutePath as resolvePath(this.cwd, path); JsonlSessionRepo.resolveCreateDestination (dist/harness/session/jsonl/repo.js:172) and list({cwd}) both pass the session cwd through it, so the FileSystem Nomi hands to pi is the one place that decides how a lane identity resolves.

invariants: A lane identity written into a session header is byte-identical on every platform and every drive
A freshly opened project lists its 'main' conversation before the user types
Input that cannot be admitted fails with a named lane code the panel renders, never a silent null

invariant_owner_layer.why: createLaneFileSystem is the only FileSystem pi receives for lane sessions and therefore the only resolver of session cwd; keeping identities under LANE_IDENTITY_ROOT verbatim there fixes create, list, delete and trace reads at once. LANE_IDENTITY_ROOT is defined once, next to the resolver that must keep it verbatim (laneFileSystem.mts); laneSession.mts builds identities from it and filters lists with it. prepareInput is the single admission step every composer send passes.

door_reduction.why_not: laneSessionCwd has one writer (laneSession.mts); createLaneFileSystem is defined in laneFileSystem.mts and constructed only by laneSession.mts. The prepareInput doors in laneDesktopRuntime.ts are a different function of the same name (main-process input preparation), unrelated to renderer admission; the renderer has one definition (laneClient) and one composer caller (useAgentPanelV4Actions).

generality_proof: The identity is resolved in exactly one place for all four session operations (create, list, delete, trace), so no lane command can see a host-resolved identity again; and every composer send now passes an admission step that either returns an address or throws a lane code the panel already translates (agent_lane_closed).

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Returns lane identities under LANE_IDENTITY_ROOT verbatim from absolutePath; everything else keeps pi's host resolution.
Returns the conversation to admit input into, or throws agent_lane_closed.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Filters with the same LANE_IDENTITY_ROOT and lists through the same repo FileSystem; on Windows it previously threw agent_lane_conversation_missing for every lane, which emptied the agent section of feedback bundles.
Creates through openLaneSession, so new migrations write the canonical identity.
Resolves real project file paths, not lane identities; host resolution is correct there.
Hashes the session directory name it is given; with the fix the name is the same on every platform.

recurrence.reason: Every Windows user hits it on every send in every project; it would return with any new virtual identity handed to a host resolver or any admission path that turns failure into null.
same_class_scan: rg 'laneSessionCwd|nomi-lane/|CWD_PREFIX' electron src scripts: one identity owner (laneSession.mts), four consumers, all behind the same FileSystem
rg 'absolutePath' electron: only laneCodingPaths (real paths) besides pi's own calls
Full tests/agent-runtime suite run on Windows after the fix

prevention.invariant: Lane identities are never resolved against the host; admission never answers with a silent null
prevention.failure_mode: A regression shows up on Linux CI through lane-identity-host-path.test.mts, which replaces host resolution with Windows semantics for identity strings, and in laneClient.test.ts for the silent null.
prevention.strategy: Keep the identity verbatim in the one FileSystem pi gets; make admission failures named; the Windows release checklist (docs/release-process.md §4) now includes a real-model agent send on the RC build. The agent-runtime suite is not yet wired into win-gate: about 19 cases are still red on Windows under Electron's Node and are being triaged into test-only POSIX assumptions vs product defects first.

legacy_paths.rationale: The separate CWD_PREFIX literal in laneSession.mts is gone; the identity root is one constant in laneFileSystem.mts used by the FileSystem, the identity function, the list filter and the trace filter. prepareInput no longer has a null branch.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: pi's host resolution is correct for real paths; the defect was ours for treating an identity as a path. No upstream change needed.

migration: No migration. Sessions written by v0.22.0 on Windows (header cwd '<drive>:\nomi-lane\<name>', directory '--<drive>--nomi-lane-<name>--') stay on disk untouched and are not listed. The agent could never send on those builds, so such sessions hold at most history that 0.22.0's legacy migration copied in; the original legacy files remain in .nomi/legacy-archive/. v0.22.0 was withdrawn after a few installs.
residual_risks: A Windows user who ran v0.22.0 on a project with pre-lane agent history will not see that migrated history in the list (files remain on disk and in legacy-archive).
The real-model check covers apimart DeepSeek V4 Pro only; other text vendors share the same admission path.
